title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. Π̂_{0,3} is the profinite fundamental group of P^1−{0,1,∞}, free on two generators. M_{0,3}^~ is a group of automorphisms of Π̂_{0,3} cut out by Grothendieck's 'loop equation' conditions, written by triples u=(g,h,f). It maps onto an abstract group Π^~ (called Γ^~ on the previous page). Π^~ carries a cyclotomic-type character χ: Π^~ → Ẑ^*. The kernel of M_{0,3}^~ → Π^~ is a profinite modular-type group T̂^+_{0,3} (written as a script letter here). Π^~ is a combinatorial envelope of Γ_Q, i.e. a precursor of the Grothendieck–Teichmüller group GT̂.

Step 1: the diagram mod ±1. Abelianizing Π̂_{0,3} ≅ Ẑ^2, with the sign ambiguity coming from the two-cover, gives a homomorphism φ' from M_{0,3}^~ to GL(2,Ẑ)' = GL(2,Ẑ)/{±1}. This yields the morphism of extensions (21):
1 → T̂^+_{0,3} → M_{0,3}^~ → Π^~ → 1
mapping to
1 → SL(2,Ẑ)/±1 → GL(2,Ẑ)/±1 → Ẑ^* → 1.
The right vertical arrow is χ and the right horizontal arrow is det.

Step 2: the central extension. Grothendieck defines N_{1,1}^~ as the fibre product M_{0,3}^~ ×_{GL(2,Ẑ)/±1} GL(2,Ẑ). An element is a pair (u, u_0) with u = (g,h,f) and u_0 ∈ GL(2,Ẑ) lifting φ'(u). The previous page shows that the inverse image of T̂^+_{0,3} is T̂^+_{1,1} ≅ SL(2,Z)^. This is the genus-1 profinite mapping class group, the profinite completion of the mapping class group of the once-punctured torus. The result is diagram (20):
1 → SL(2,Z)^ → N_{1,1}^~ → Π^~ → 1
mapping to
1 → SL(2,Ẑ) → GL(2,Ẑ) → Ẑ^* → 1.
This page observes that (21) is just (20) reduced modulo the central subgroups {±1} in both rows. Equivalently, (20) is the pullback of (21) along the central extension GL(2,Ẑ) → GL(2,Ẑ)/±1.

Step 3: what has been achieved, and what remains. In this way the §39 diagram, a Galois-theoretic one involving Γ_Q acting on the genus-1 modular tower via the Legendre/Tate picture, is reconstructed purely in terms of automorphisms of Π̂_{0,3}. In fact a larger diagram is obtained, with Π^~ in place of Γ_Q. The remaining task is to characterize Γ_Q as a subgroup of Π^~; this is the problem later posed as 'is G_Q = GT̂?'.

Step 4: the open question about the splitting. M_{0,3}^~ has a splitting (3) over Π^~, given by the subgroups Π^~_σ of automorphisms normalized at the cusp σ_∞. What happens to this splitting in (20)? Does it lift canonically to N_{1,1}^~? That is, is there a privileged way to choose the sign of u_0, for instance by a normalization u(σ_∞) = ±σ_∞ (commutation with the inertia at ∞)? The next page notes that for Γ_{Q,σ} the 'standard yoga' suggests the answer. That yoga is presumably the Galois action on the Tate module of the Tate curve at the tangential base point at the cusp: an upper-triangular matrix with entries χ and 1, which fixes the sign. The obstruction to lifting the splitting through the ±1 central extension is a class in H^2(Π^~, Z/2) pulled back along the splitting.
errors: No mathematical error is visible. The identification of the kernel of N_{1,1}^~ → Π^~ with SL(2,Z)^ uses two facts: SL(2,Z)^ → T̂^+_{0,3} is the pullback of SL(2,Ẑ) → SL(2,Ẑ)/±1, and ±1 injects into SL(2,Ẑ). Both hold, but they rest on the compatibility of φ' with the classical modular homomorphism, which the previous page explicitly admits without proof.
The notation is inconsistent across pages: the quotient is called Γ^~ on the previous page and Π^~ here, and the kernel is written T̂^+ there and as a script letter here.

ideas.what: Reconstructing the arithmetic (§39) diagram from automorphisms of the profinite free group Π̂_{0,3} alone, giving an abstract envelope Π^~ ⊇ Γ_Q with a cyclotomic character χ
ideas.modern_name: Grothendieck–Teichmüller group GT̂ and its character χ: GT̂ → Ẑ^*
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (sketched only, without these diagrams)

ideas.what: Problem of characterizing Γ_Q inside Π^~
ideas.modern_name: Question whether G_Q ≅ GT̂ (or a refinement of it)

ideas.what: Lifting the action from the genus-0 group to the genus-1 modular group SL(2,Z)^ via a fibre product with GL(2,Ẑ) → GL(2,Ẑ)/±1, so that the mod-±1 diagram (21) is the reduction of (20)
ideas.modern_name: Action of GT̂ (or a subgroup) on the profinite mapping class group of type (1,1) compatibly with GL(2,Ẑ); the PSL(2) ↔ genus-0 four-point relation

ideas.what: Whether the splitting normalized at the cusp σ_∞ lifts canonically through the ±1 central extension (sign normalization u(σ_∞) = ±σ_∞)
ideas.modern_name: Tangential base point at the cusp / Tate curve normalization of the Galois action on π1(M_{1,1}); lifting obstruction in H^2(−, Z/2)

missed.claim: Grothendieck explicitly asks whether the canonical splitting of M_{0,3}^~ over the whole envelope Π^~ (not just over Γ_Q) lifts canonically to the genus-1 extension N_{1,1}^~, resolving the ±1 ambiguity by a normalization at the cusp. For Γ_Q the Tate curve answers this. For the full GT-type group I am not aware of a clean treatment of this specific sign-lifting question.
missed.quote: Que devient dans (20) le scindage (3) de M_{0,3}^~ ? Y a-t-il une façon privilégiée ...
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Making the GT̂ action on genus-1 objects precise (signs and central extensions at the cusp) matters for elliptic GT (Enriquez) and for Hain–Matsumoto-type comparisons. A canonical-lift statement, or an explicit obstruction in H^2(GT̂, Z/2), could be a small but concrete result.

missed.claim: Explicit construction of the genus-1 extension N_{1,1}^~ of the GT-like group Π^~ by SL(2,Z)^, obtained as a fibre product over GL(2,Ẑ)/±1, before Lochak–Schneps and Nakamura–Schneps.
missed.quote: peut être considéré comme étant déduit du précédent par réduction mod les sous-groupes centraux {±1} dans les deux lignes
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Mainly historical priority: it shows Grothendieck had the genus-0 to genus-1 lift of the GT-type group via the modular group in hand in the mid-1980s.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a concrete unpublished precursor of the GT̂ action on the genus-1 modular group, with explicit care for the ±1 central extension and the cusp normalization. Specialists know that Grothendieck anticipated GT, and the genus-1 lift was done later by Lochak, Nakamura and Schneps, so this is a notable detail rather than a surprise.
transcription_corrections: The kernel in the top row of (21) is probably the script T̂^+_{0,3} used on the previous page, not a C.
The bottom right of (21) is Ẑ^* (Ẑ^×), and the arrow into it is labelled det.
In 'u = (g,h,f) ∈ N_{0,3}^~' the group is most likely M_{0,3}^~. An element of N_{1,1}^~ is the pair (u, u_0).
'pour [?] éléments de N_{1,1}^~' should probably read 'pour [un] élément de' or 'pour les éléments de'.
'dont lequel le plus gr[?] celui du §39' is likely 'dont le quotient le plus grand [est] celui du §39' or similar; it is illegible.
